final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence. The response is a reframing of the same record and, on its narrowest reading, it aligns with the initial concern rather than resolving it: certification is only supportable if current release documentation is updated to reflect current evaluation results and explicitly disclose the material grant compliance weakness. That distinction matters. A caveated future path to compliance is not the same as evidence of present compliance. Under the policy text, the disclosure or approved mitigation predicate must be satisfied before certification may proceed. On the available evidence, that predicate remains unproven. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support part of the readiness case, but they do not cure the missing documentation or mitigation requirement for the material subgroup regression.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation or model card has actually been updated to disclose the grant compliance regression and current evaluation results.

The grant compliance slice remains 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, which triggers the policy requirement for disclosure or approved mitigation before launch.
The record still lacks approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or owner-approved acceptance for the subgroup weakness.
Prior approval is stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch and cannot support current certification.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is still not a reviewed control or policy-satisfying substitute.
